answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the spiral reward in the sable ledger costs the operator directly, and the whisper audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 22% of the resulting slash, which burns for adversarial review out of the copycat's own capital. A farm of 273 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the swarm makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
